question: Should OpenClaw accept this experiment-gated core `claws update` planning and integrity/consent schema as the shared lifecycle contract before the stacked apply PR is considered?
rationale: This creates a new CLI and host-facing consent model rather than repairing an established behavior; automated review cannot decide the intended permanent core boundary or approval semantics.

options.title: Sponsor the planner contract
options.body: Accept the read-only planner as the core experimental primitive after final runtime proof and normal code review.

options.title: Narrow the core contract
options.body: Keep only generic planning and ownership seams in core, moving host-specific capability-consent presentation behind a later owner-approved surface.

options.title: Pause the stack
options.body: Defer the planner and dependent apply work until the Claw lifecycle RFC or an owner decision establishes the desired product boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the planner contract
recommendation.body: Accept the read-only planner as the core experimental primitive after final runtime proof and normal code review.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review defines the principal planner safety and provenance invariants in this stack.
